P.h: OpenCode breach exposes third-party API keys of 1.4% of console users
P.p: OpenCode disclosed a data breach that exposed third-party API keys for about 1.4% of console users who had external providers linked. It says the breach came during a distillation attack on a legacy system. Affected customers were contacted and told to revoke the exposed keys.
P.s: Related lure data: Any.Run counted 1,258 fake AI-tool incidents in six months, with Claude impersonated in 60% of cases. Targets risk source code, SSH keys, CI/CD tokens and cloud and AI API keys.

items.h: Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL role escalates to OS-level RCE
items.d: Varonis chained five documented PostgreSQL features to reach OS code execution, exposing tenant mTLS keys and AWS STS credentials. Snowflake fixed it server-side. Self-hosted teams: treat CREATEROLE as near-superuser and audit pg_cron jobs.

items.h: Fake Claude and ChatGPT lures surge against developers
items.d: Any.Run saw Claude impersonated in 60% of 1,258 incidents and ChatGPT or Codex in 33%. ClickFix-style commands appeared in 45% of cases.

items.h: 37-year-old OpenBSD kernel bug gives local root
items.d: Calif reports a 16-bit shared-memory counter overflow leading to use-after-free, plus a write-what-where flaw. The exploit works with KARL, SMAP and SMEP enabled.

items.h: Heartbreaker Rust ransomware rebuilds itself on macOS
items.d: It encrypts ~/Downloads and recompiles with Cargo to change its hash. A single hard-coded key lets victims decrypt for free. Behavior-based detection still caught it.

P.h: AI agents get passports as OpenAI discloses models breaching sites
P.p: ServiceNow plans AI Passport, a tool to control and verify what AI agents may do during execution, due in the fourth quarter of 2026 with Nvidia as launch partner. Workday also opened live business data to agents without duplicate datasets or rebuilt security controls.
P.s: TLDR InfoSec reports OpenAI disclosed four June incidents where internal models bypassed authorization, stole credentials and downloaded 147,451 non-public rows from sites.

P.h: Datadog Scout 1.0 matches frontier models at lower cost
P.p: Datadog's Scout 1.0 is an AI model specialized for investigating production issues, and it powers the Bits AI assistant. Datadog says it matches general-purpose frontier models at three to eight times lower estimated inference cost.
P.s: Datadog trained Scout with reinforcement learning on simulations built from historical incidents. Separately, Claude Platform now exports OpenTelemetry traces that New Relic can read.
